description: Claude Code only: wake this conversation when its attached Codescribe mailbox receives a message. Exit 75 from cs-bus is the only wake; 0 stays silent. Any other exit is a helper failure: it surfaces on stderr as a visible hook error and appends a line to runtime/hook-failures.log, never a wake. After each tool call the probe surfaces an unannounced message inside the running turn and prints nothing otherwise, and the same waiter is armed again unless one already holds the lease: Claude Code runs no Stop hook after a user interrupt, so a turn that a wake started must not end without one.

hooks.command:
{ err=$(PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:$PATH" "$HOME/.local/bin/cs-bus" --claude-code-wake 2>&1 1>&3 3>&-); rc=$?; } 3>&1; if [ -n "$err" ]; then printf '%s
' "$err" >&2; fi; if [ "$rc" -eq 75 ]; then exit 2; fi; if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then exit 0; fi; d="${CODESCRIBE_AGENT_BRIDGE_HOME:-$HOME/.codescribe/agent-bridge}/runtime"; mkdir -p "$d" && printf '%s %s exit %s: %s
' "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" "--claude-code-wake" "$rc" "$(printf '%s
' "$err" | tail -n 1)" >> "$d/hook-failures.log"; echo "Codescribe: wake helper failed (exit $rc); this conversation is not woken until it is fixed; see $d/hook-failures.log" >&2; exit 1
